payload.rebuttal: fixed: Correct that create_task's row and task_created fact are already committed when the run_created append runs, so a refusal there raises with the task live and the record short one fact. I did not make this atomic: the Record protocol (saffron/record/contract.py, forbidden to this spec) appends one fact at a time with no transactional pairing, and finish_run and record_findings already carry the identical commit-then-append risk by the same design, accepted and tested elsewhere. What I added is test_a_refused_run_created_still_leaves_the_task_created in tests/test_ledger_events.py, which drives this exact case and asserts the task row survives, task_created alone is recorded, and RecordError propagates. That documents the gap precisely instead of leaving it silently undetected, within what this spec's touches allow.
